ca_5_ribbon_falls_amphitheater.blurb: A big granite bowl on the north side of Yosemite Valley, tucked beneath Ribbon Falls and facing across to the West Face of El Capitan. This is long-route territory: multi-pitch trad lines and aid climbs, some stretching to ten pitches, split about evenly between free and aided. The free grades cluster around 5.9 and 5.10, with a few easier lines in the 5.6 to 5.8 range and a single 5.11 and 5.12 at the top end. Expect a faint, bushy approach, vegetation to clear on some pitches, and few other parties. It suits experienced wall and crack climbers who are comfortable with route-finding.

ca_zena_rocks.blurb: Zena Rocks is a group of wide slabs lining the western edge of Middle Earth valley on Fairview Mountain, in the high desert around Apple Valley. Fifteen routes, nine sport and six trad, run from 5.6 up to 5.10, with most falling between 5.7 and 5.10. Lines are roughly 80 to 100 feet, making them some of the longer pitches at Fairview. The walls face northeast and get decent shelter from the wind. Expect smooth slab with cracks and edges; friction is good but can turn slick when sand blows in. Cooler months are the comfortable time to visit, and there is little shade or water.

ca_top_gun_boulders.blurb: A cluster of neighbouring outcrop boulders along the north rim of Happy Boulders, in the Volcanic Tablelands north of Bishop. Fifteen problems here, mostly V0 with a spread up through V3 and a single V4, so it is friendlier than much of the canyon. A handful are tall enough to feel highball. The boulders face south, which makes this a good pick on cold, sunny days and a poor one in midsummer heat. Landings in the surrounding canyon are generally flat, and the area suits mixed groups and anyone warming up before harder problems nearby.

ca_steel_monkey_wall.blurb: A steep wall of roughly 70 feet in The Benches section of the Emeralds, beside the South Yuba River off the I-80 corridor. Mostly sport climbing: twelve sport lines, two top-rope and one trad. The grades lean hard, with a concentration from 5.11 to 5.13 and only a few easier lines near 5.6 to 5.8. The wall faces mostly north and stays in shade, so it works on warm days when sunnier crags are uncomfortable. The walk from the river parking is around fifteen minutes on a fire road and a short cut through trees.

ca_predator_wall_south_face.blurb: The steeper, more technical face of Predator Wall in the high desert near Barstow, within the New Jack City and Box Canyon West zone. All fifteen routes are sport climbs and the grades start at 5.10 and run into the low 5.13s, with the bulk between 5.11 and 5.12. Expect sustained, steep climbing on sharp edges, long pitches, and fewer people than at busier desert crags. The face points south, so it is a good cold-weather choice and gets hot later in the day. Bring a standard sport rack and a helmet, and keep an eye out for loose holds near the tops.
ca_predator_wall_south_face.approach: A short walk up from where the road ends at the canyon mouth, around 5 to 10 minutes over uneven, rocky ground.
